objectives.text: The data are used to monitor an individual organization's overall liquidity profile for institutions supervised by the Federal Reserve, providing detailed information on liquidity risks within different business lines.

citations.quote: The data are used to monitor an individual organization's overall liquidity profile for institutions supervised by the Federal Reserve. These data also provide detailed information on the liquidity risks within different business lines

objectives.text: The data serve as part of the Federal Reserve's supervisory surveillance program in liquidity risk management, providing timely information on firm-specific liquidity risks during periods of stress.

citations.quote: the data serve as part of the Federal Reserve's supervisory surveillance program in its liquidity risk management area and provide timely information on firm-specific liquidity risks during periods of stress.

objectives.text: The report responds to the need, highlighted by the 2007-2008 financial crisis, for timely liquidity data to identify and monitor liquidity risks at individual firms and in aggregate across the financial system.

citations.quote: The financial crisis of 2007 and 2008 highlighted the need for timely liquidity data to identify and monitor liquidity risks at individual firms as well as in aggregate across the financial system.

objectives.text: Capturing intra-company flows and exposures via disaggregated, legal-entity-level views (rather than a single consolidated view) is a focus of the report, to identify vulnerabilities posed by potential impediments to the movement of liquidity across legal entities.

citations.quote: A single, consolidated view is not sufficient to provide meaningful insight into an institution's liquidity profile. Rather, disaggregated views by legal entities (parent company, broker/dealer entities, bank entities etc.) have contributed to supervisory monitoring efforts and risk supervision by identifying vulnerabilities posed by potential impediments to the movement of liquidity across legal entities.

definitions.definition: Collects quantitative information on selected assets, liabilities, funding activities, and contingent liabilities on a consolidated basis and by material entity subsidiary; comprises sections covering broad funding classifications by product, outstanding balance and purpose, segmented by maturity date.

citations.quote: The FR 2052a report collects quantitative information on selected assets, liabilities, funding activities, and contingent liabilities on a consolidated basis and by material entity subsidiary. The FR 2052a comprises sections covering broad funding classifications by product, outstanding balance and purpose, segmented by maturity date.

notes: This source is the Federal Reserve's public description page for the FR 2052a form (not the full instructions/reporting schedules), so only the timing/granularity/reporting-frequency and confidentiality content bears directly on the ratified scope (liquidity reporting's contribution to detection speed). Frequency tiers and thresholds ($100 billion assets; $75 billion short-term wholesale funding; Category I-IV) are reproduced exactly as given; the source itself does not define 'Category I, II, III, or IV standards,' 'material entity subsidiary,' or 'average weighted short-term wholesale funding,' so these are recorded as undefined-here per the definitions rule. No content in this source addresses discount-window/FHLB interoperability, discount-window stigma, Call Report timing specifically, or the Hsu/McKernan reform proposals; such topics are outside what this particular item contains and are not fabricated here. The monthly-vs-daily reporting cadence and the Board's only-temporary/discretionary authority to accelerate frequency during stress, plus the non-publication of micro data, are preserved verbatim as structural features relevant to the defect register without characterizing them further, per the fidelity rule.
